title: Take-up Rate for Lasting Power of Attorney
what_it_is: Take-up Rate for Lasting Power of Attorney

sections.label: LPA applications and fee waiver
sections.summary: Since March 2010 over 20,000 LPAs were received, with about 8,360 accepted in 2015, a 160% rise from 2014, and the $50 fee waived for Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Since the Mental Capacity Act came into effect in March 2010, we have received more than 20,000 LPAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In 2015 alone, we accepted about 8,360 LPAs, which is an increase of almost 160% from 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For Singapore Citizens, we waived the $50 application fee for the most common LPA form used.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In addition, we secured the support of SingPost for a free postal service for the public to submit LPA applications via Business Reply Service envelopes.

sections.label: Feedback on MediShield option
sections.summary: Feedback says the MediShield option is very good, and options with MediShield Life and Pioneer Generation ambassadors would be considered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have got feedback that the MediShield one is really very good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We would be happy to consider those options, as the Member pointed out, with MediShield Life and also even our Pioneer Generation ambassadors.

sections.label: LPA age distribution and outreach
sections.summary: LPA take-up is clustered around those post-50, and the Pioneer Generation Office and its ambassadors could be leveraged to advise the Pioneer Generation on LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last of all, maybe the Minister can consider leveraging on the Pioneer Generation Office (PGO) when they reach out to the Pioneer Generation to advise them on the LPA as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Those 21 to 34 years of age, we have about 3%; 35 to 55, about 28%; 56 to 70, 41%; 71 to 85, 24%; and above 85, about 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It is largely clustered around those who are, perhaps, post-50 and above, which is very natural when we begin to think of those issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: But we encourage more Singaporeans to consider doing this early because you never know when conditions may deteriorate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In fact, the feedback from the public as well as from the Office, the Pioneer Generation ambassadors have been doing a great job in terms of engaging the elderly, as well as informing them of some of these key policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We also do not want to overly burden them with too many things but they are a ready resource base that we should draw on and this is something that we should work on.
